read: Inspect repository worktree text with file, list, or search, or use show with side head for committed text. No comparison base is configured; diff and show(base) are unavailable. File and show accept path and optional offset/limit; list accepts optional path/limit; search requires a literal query (not a regex) and accepts optional path/limit. File/show offsets are one-based lines. On truncation follow next_offset for file/show; narrow other requests.
write: Apply one unified diff to one repository-relative text file. Hunk line counts are taken from the hunk body. A hunk whose context and removed lines do not match at its `@@` start line applies only where they match exactly one place in the file; copy those lines exactly and add context when they repeat. A hunk with only `+` lines needs a `-N,0` header to insert after line N. To create an empty file, use only `--- /dev/null` and `+++ b/<path>` headers.
bash_none: Run Bash directly on the host without a sandbox. Commands run with the host process's own access; writes and network access are not restricted by the harness. Output and duration are bounded; long output keeps each stream's start and end. Applied writes are not rolled back.
read_with_base: Inspect the repository with one bounded read-only action. Use `file` with `path` and optional `offset`/`limit` for worktree text; `list` with optional `path`/`limit`; `search` with `query` and optional `path`/`limit`; `diff` with optional `path` for changes from the host-selected commit; or `show` with `path`, `side` (`base` or `head`), and optional `offset`/`limit`. Search queries are literal strings, not regular expressions. File/show offsets are one-based line numbers and limits count lines. If truncated, continue file/show at next_offset; narrow list/search/diff when no continuation is supplied. Comparison base OID: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111.
bash_file_system: Run Bash inside a host filesystem sandbox. Workspace reads are allowed; writes require host grants. Network access is not restricted by the harness. Git metadata is read-only: `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log` work, but staging, committing, stashing, and creating or switching branches fail. Do not retry them; the host commits your changes after the turn. Output and duration are bounded; long output keeps each stream's start and end. Applied writes are not rolled back.
bash_file_system_and_network: Run Bash inside the host sandbox. Workspace reads are allowed; writes require host grants. Network access is denied. Git metadata is read-only: `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log` work, but staging, committing, stashing, and creating or switching branches fail. Do not retry them; the host commits your changes after the turn. Output and duration are bounded; long output keeps each stream's start and end. Applied writes are not rolled back.
